findings.title: Duplicate IV inverter nn_pricer._bs_iv_vectorized (undamped Newton) silently fails in the OTM-call wing; it shapes the published Greeks surface ('69 nodes', '3 unstable nodes') and the NN accuracy claim
findings.description: The repo has two Black-Scholes IV inverters that give different answers. heston.implied_vol_from_price uses brentq and is correct. nn_pricer._bs_iv_vectorized uses plain Newton: Brenner-Subrahmanyam start, sigma clipped to [1e-4, 5], and one convergence test applied to the whole batch. For OTM calls it starts at about 0.05 vol, where vega is close to 0. The step overshoots to 5.0, then to 1e-4, and keeps bouncing between them. After 50 iterations it returns the clip value as if it were a valid IV and does not set NaN. risk_monitor uses this inverter to build the published Greeks surface and then drops any IV below 0.005, so the failed nodes disappear without a warning. The NN training data and NN benchmark use the same inverter and filter, so the advertised NN MAE is measured only where the inverter happened to work.
findings.evidence:
(1) BS round-trip grid in a private copy (T 7d-2y, ln(K/S) -0.6..0.4, sigma 0.08-2.0, 1,163 cases with price above intrinsic): brentq gave 0 NaN and max error 2.5e-7. Newton gave 85 cases off by more than 1e-4, with max error 0.5999. Examples: T=14d K=102.5 true 0.15 -> 0.0457; T=30d K=105 true 0.08 -> 0.0001.
(2) Published greeks_surface.parquet: rebuilt from joint_cal_2026-03-24.pkl params (median diff to the published IVs 4.5e-5). Newton keeps exactly 69 of the 90-node grid, which is the published '69 nodes'. It is wrong at 23 nodes, 11 of them with model price above $1. Example: 365d K/F=e^0.171, price $152.66, Newton 0.0001, brentq 0.1997.
(3) Recomputing vomma z-scores over all 90 nodes with brentq IVs gives 5 unstable nodes, all in the 180d/365d OTM-call wing: (180d, 0.132), (180d, 0.171), (365d, 0.171), (365d, 0.211), (365d, 0.25), with z up to 4.47. The published 3 nodes are 365d at lm -0.30, -0.26 and +0.13, and greeks.html:129 hard-codes 'All three unstable nodes are at the 1-year maturity'.
(4) NN benchmark (nn_pricer.benchmark, seed 42, 500 options, T=0.25): 194 of 500 options (every strike with K/F > 1.08, prices up to $73.55) fail the ground-truth inversion and are excluded from the published 'MAE < 0.07 vp'.
(5) NN training region (150 parameter sets x 100 options): 2,186 of 14,996 Newton IVs (14.6%) disagree with brentq by more than 0.1 vp. Most are dropped by the [0.02, 3] filter. 21 survive as wrong labels, with errors up to 12 vp (e.g. T=0.058 x=0.125: 0.060 vs 0.186).
findings.proposed_fix: Delete _bs_iv_vectorized and expose one vectorised inverter in a new joint_vol_calibration/models/black_scholes.py. Use it from heston, risk_monitor, nn_pricer and joint_calibrator. Make it safeguarded Newton with bisection fallback, keep a per-element bracket [lo, hi] that is updated every step, start from Manaster-Koehler sigma0 = sqrt(2|ln(F/K)|/T), and return NaN per element when it has not converged (|price residual| > tol). Price OTM options only: puts for K<F, calls for K>F. Mask nodes whose model price is below the Heston integrator's absolute accuracy (~1e-3, since deep-wing prices of ~3e-4 are noise). Then regenerate greeks_surface.parquet, NN training data and the benchmark, and replace the hard-coded '69 nodes', '6 maturities' and 'All three unstable nodes...' text with values computed from the data. Tests: (a) property test over the grid above comparing to brentq, max error < 1e-6 and no clip values returned; (b) regression test that 365d, K=F*e^0.1714 under the 03-24 params inverts to 0.1997 +/- 1e-4; (c) assert risk_monitor returns 90 nodes for the default grid.

findings.title: `python dashboard/app.py` overwrites the tracked regime_labels.parquet with demoted XGBoost predictions; prior fix 90dc851 covered only cloud_refresh
findings.description: Commit 90dc851 fixed the bot appending clf.predict() output to regime_labels.parquet by switching cloud_refresh.extend_regime_labels to rule labels. The same defect is still present in the web app, in a worse form. _startup_data_refresh runs whenever the newest SPX row in the DB is more than 3 days old. It calls DataPipeline.daily_refresh() (network) and then _refresh_regime_labels(). That function loads regime_classifier.pkl and REWRITES the whole parquet with clf.predict_series(feats) in-sample, truncated to the DB's last date. The committed DB's SPX data ends 2026-06-18, so this runs on every fresh clone that follows the README quickstart. It silently replaces the deterministic rule labels (which the front page headlines and the tests pin) with the classifier that C16/C17 demoted, and it modifies tracked artifacts (the parquet, plus options rows inserted into the DB). The guard test only greps scripts/cloud_refresh.py, so it cannot see this path.
findings.proposed_fix: Delete _refresh_regime_labels. Move the rule-label logic from cloud_refresh.extend_regime_labels into the package (e.g. joint_vol_calibration/signals/labels.py) and have both the bot and any refresh path call that one function. Make the dashboard's background refresh opt-in (env VOL_DASH_LIVE_REFRESH=1, default off) and point it at a scratch DB, never the tracked data_store. Replace the source-grep test with a behavioural one: run _startup_data_refresh with DataPipeline mocked to a no-op and assert the parquet hash is unchanged. Also add a repo-wide check that no module calls predict_series and then to_parquet on regime_labels.

findings.title: Prior fix 35690a2 incomplete: the gate checks VIX tenors but not SPX expiries, so the selector now headlines a 9-option, single-expiry fit (RMSE 0.041 vp)
findings.description: 35690a2 found that ranking archived fits by SPX RMSE rewards under-identified data (1 VIX tenor gives a spuriously excellent fit) and added an n_vix_tenors >= 3 gate. The same pathology has come back on the SPX side, and the gate has no term for it. Since the daily SPX chain collapsed to one usable expiry (the known outage), every accepted fit has 9 SPX options, i.e. 9 vega anchors in one expiry. Fitting 5 Heston parameters to a single smile slice gives tiny RMSE, and latest_good_calibration_path() picks the minimum RMSE. The live headline therefore moved from the documented 2026-07-01 fit (54 options, 0.375 vp) to a single-expiry fit, with no warning. This is cross-referenced with the outage auditor: the new evidence here is that these fits pass the gate and are PUBLISHED.
findings.evidence:
Remote pickles (inspected with a restricted unpickler that allows only numpy scalar/dtype): 09-25 n_spx_options=9 RMSE 0.041; 09-28 9, 0.649; 10-02 9, 0.195; 10-07 9, 0.295; 10-09 9, 1.796; local 09-11 9, 0.215 with kappa 5.000. All have n_vix_tenors=4. 07-01 has 54 options and RMSE 0.375.
GitHub Actions job 114096310910 (2026-10-10): 'SPX surface: 9 liquid options across 1 expiries' ... 'Done (accepted): kappa=3.0457 ... 9 SPX opts, 4 VIX tenors'.
Live https://navnoorbawa.me/calibration.html badge: '2026-09-25 · SPX = 7743.4 · r = 4.07%'.
is_acceptable_calibration only checks sigma, rho, kappa bounds, RMSE > 3 and n_vix_tenors.
findings.proposed_fix: Persist n_spx_expiries in JointCalibrator.calibrate(). In is_acceptable_calibration require n_spx_expiries >= 3 and n_spx_options >= 27, and treat a missing count as reject for post-09-05 files. In latest_good_calibration_path apply the sufficiency gate first, then prefer the newest sufficient fit within N days, or rank by RMSE normalised by degrees of freedom, not raw RMSE. Show a 'calibration is N days old' banner when the headline is stale. Test: a fixture pickle set (07-01 with 54/4 and 09-25 with 9/4, 1 expiry) must select 07-01.

findings.title: Daily fits are priced with hard-coded r=4.5%, q=1.3%, but the pickle and page report r = ^IRX (4.07%, labelled 'USD 6M SOFR') and q = 0.0%
findings.description: There are three disagreeing rate sources for one fit. cloud_refresh constructs JointCalibrator(as_of_date=TODAY) without r or q, so pricing, forwards and IV inversion all use the constructor defaults r=0.045, q=0.013. After the fit it overwrites result['r'] = get_tbill_rate(TODAY) and never stores q, because calibrate() does not return r or q. The dashboard then shows r = T-bill and q = cal.get('q', 0) = 0.00%. The template hard-codes the source as 'USD 6M SOFR (2026-03)'. Anyone who re-prices from the stored parameters with the stored r and q gets a different forward drift (r-q = 4.07% instead of 3.2%) from the one actually fitted.
findings.evidence:
Pickles: 09-11 r=0.03913 with no 'q' key; 08-27..09-04 r=0.0369..0.0377 with no q.
JointCalibrator.__init__(r: float = 0.045, q: float = 0.013) at joint_calibrator.py:477-478.
cloud_refresh.py:308 calls `cal = JointCalibrator(as_of_date=TODAY)` and line 315 sets `result["r"] = get_tbill_rate(TODAY)`.
Live calibration.html: 'Risk-free rate r 4.07% USD 6M SOFR (2026-03) · Dividend yield q 0.0%'.
findings.proposed_fix: In cloud_refresh: r = get_tbill_rate(spot_date); q = config.SPX_DIV_YIELD (new constant); call JointCalibrator(as_of_date=..., r=r, q=q). Have calibrate() include 'r', 'q' and 'rate_source' in its result, and stop overwriting after the fit. Template: show '3M T-bill (^IRX) {{date}}' and the stored q. Test: monkeypatch get_tbill_rate to 0.04 and assert the calibrator saw r=0.04 and the result stores r=0.04, q=0.013.

findings.title: 74 broad excepts swallow errors into *_error keys that no template renders; freeze_site only greps 'Traceback', so a broken artifact publishes as an empty page with status OK
findings.description: Every loader in app.py catches Exception and writes d['<x>_error'] = str(e). Of the 10 keys (db/regime/pdv/cal/smile/greeks/eq/pkl/ann/wf), none is referenced by any template, so the errors are invisible. Fallbacks substitute zeros and hard-coded values: calib_date falls back to '2026-05-31', and greeks.html hard-codes '6 maturities', 'Across all 69 nodes' and 'All three unstable nodes are at the 1-year maturity'. freeze_site.py, which is the only publish gate in the unattended daily job, counts a page as broken only if it returns non-200 or contains 'Traceback'. So the most likely failures (a missing or unreadable artifact) pass and get published. The calibration error fallback itself is untested and crashes: kappa=0 reaches '0.693/d.kappa*252' in the template.
findings.evidence:
Private copy with greeks_surface.parquet removed and joint_cal_*.pkl corrupted, then `python dashboard/freeze_site.py <tmp>`:
- 'OK /greeks -> greeks.html 33852 bytes status=200'. The page reads '0 nodes · 6 maturities ... Unstable Nodes 0 / 0 ... Mean Vomma 0 Across all 69 nodes ... All three unstable nodes are at the 1-year maturity'.
- index.html silently shows 'Calibration: 2026-05-31'.
- /calibration returns 500 with ZeroDivisionError at calibration.html:105 (the fallback path).
`grep -c _error dashboard/templates/*.html` gives 0 for every template. ruff BLE001: 74 in non-test code (29 in dashboard/app.py), plus 6 S110 try/except/pass in app.py.
findings.proposed_fix: Collect loader failures in d['errors'] (logged with _logger.exception) and render a visible banner from base.html. Have each route return status 500, or a response header, when d['errors'] is non-empty, and make freeze_site fail on that. Remove the hard-coded narrative numbers and the '2026-05-31' fallbacks and compute them from data. Guard divisions in templates. Add a parametrised test that deletes or corrupts each artifact in turn and asserts freeze_site exits non-zero.

findings.title: Dashboard re-implements backtest metrics with different definitions: walk-forward Sharpe still uses a flat 5% rf (the page says ^IRX), and Win Rate / N Trades / N Days differ from the engine
findings.description: C17 moved the headline Sharpe and Sortino to the engine's ^IRX hurdle (backtest.html:423 claims this). The dashboard still computes the rest with its own code: the walk-forward chart uses `rets - 0.05/252` and clips to +/-4, and the KPI row uses dashboard definitions (win rate by DAY, trade count from position diffs, n_days including the first NAV row). The 'Walk-Forward Sharpe — 6-Month OOS Windows' chart is calendar half-year slices of one full-sample run, not out-of-sample windows. BacktestEngine.walk_forward_validation exists, but its output is not used.
findings.evidence:
Recomputed from full_results.parquet and the DB ^IRX series:
- 2020-H1 Sharpe -0.12 (5%) vs +0.91 (^IRX); 2022-H1 -0.41 vs +1.25; 2020-H2 -18.0 (clipped to -4) vs -2.70; 2021-H1 -10.9 vs -2.61.
- Negative half-years: 11 vs 9. Live backtest.html shows '11/13 negative'.
KPI row (load_page4) vs engine metrics in full_results.pkl: Win Rate 28.16% vs 45.5%; N Trades 283 vs 292; N Days 1808 vs 1807. Sharpe -1.799 and Sortino -3.280 come from the engine and do match.
findings.proposed_fix: Persist all displayed metrics, including per-window walk-forward results from walk_forward_validation with rf_series, into full_results.pkl or a JSON sidecar at backtest time. Make load_page4 display those values and stop recomputing. Rename the chart to 'Half-year Sharpe (in-sample run)' unless real WF results are shown. Test: assert every KPI on the page equals the engine metric of the same name.

findings.title: Front-page research classifier is fed pdv_iv_spread = -VIX because pdv_forecast is read 130 lines before it is computed; the live feature code also differs from build_features (train/serve skew)
findings.description: load_page1 builds feat_live at line 257 with pdv_dec = (d.get('pdv_forecast') or 0)/100. d['pdv_forecast'] is only set at line 386, so the classifier always sees pdv_iv_spread = -vix. The published probabilities (prob_r0/r1/r2, clf_conf, clf_agrees) are therefore computed on a corrupted feature. The other features are also recomputed by hand: simple-return sample std from the last 30 closes, versus RMS of log returns in build_features.
findings.evidence: Wrapped the unpickled classifier to capture predict_proba input in a private copy: pdv_iv_spread fed = -0.1640. Expected (pdv 8.37 - vix 16.4)/100 = -0.0803. fear_premium was 0.9955 live vs 1.0166 from build_features for the same date (2026-06-18).
findings.proposed_fix: Compute the PDV forecast before the regime block, or better, call build_features(spx_hist, vix_wide, pdv_model=pdv) and use its last row so serving uses the training code. Test: patch the classifier, call load_page1, and assert the captured pdv_iv_spread == (pdv_forecast - vix)/100.

findings.title: Model artifacts are code-executing pickles loaded across library versions (sklearn 1.7.1 -> 1.9.1, old XGBoost config), and requirements.txt floors are wrong (FrozenEstimator needs sklearn >= 1.6)
findings.description: Every artifact is a pickle: the regime classifier (XGBoost inside CalibratedClassifierCV), PDVModel (pickles pandas internals), full_results.pkl (TradeRecord), quintic (QuinticOUParams), and the joint_cal_*.pkl files, which are plain dicts of floats. All requirements are unpinned '>=' floors, so CI and new clones load these with whatever versions are current. The loaders emit version warnings, which the libraries say can mean invalid results, and any rename of a pickled class breaks the artifact. pickle.load and torch.load(weights_only=False) also execute code. The daily bot commits pickles that the public site build then unpickles. The floors are also wrong: regime_classifier does `from sklearn.frozen import FrozenEstimator` at import time, which needs scikit-learn >= 1.6, while requirements says >=1.3.0.
findings.evidence:
Loading regime_classifier.pkl under sklearn 1.9.1 / xgboost 3.2.0 gives InconsistentVersionWarning 'from version 1.7.1 when using version 1.9.1' (x5: FrozenEstimator, IsotonicRegression x3, CalibratedClassifierCV), and XGBoost warns 'loading a serialized model ... generated by an older version ... export the model by calling Booster.save_model'. The same 4 warnings appear 13x each in the test suite.
Fresh venv with scikit-learn==1.5.2 (allowed by requirements): `from sklearn.frozen import FrozenEstimator` gives ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'sklearn.frozen'.
The NN checkpoint holds only state_dict, lists and scalars, so weights_only=True would work.
(Checked OK: numpy 1.26.4 can still load the numpy-2-written calibration pickles.)
findings.proposed_fix: (1) Calibrations: write JSON next to the pickle, as baseline_2026-03-24.json already does. The dashboard and selector read JSON; keep the pickles read-only for history. (2) Classifier: xgb_clf.get_booster().save_model('regime_xgb.json') plus the isotonic thresholds (X_thresholds_/y_thresholds_ per class) in JSON, or skops.io with a trusted-types list. (3) PDVModel: coefficients to JSON and features to parquet. (4) torch.load(..., weights_only=True). (5) Pin: commit a requirements.lock (pip-compile / uv pip compile) used by both workflows, and raise floors to scikit-learn>=1.6, xgboost>=2.1. Add a test that loads each artifact under warnings-as-errors.

findings.title: Daily job downloads ~3.4 GB of CUDA torch it never imports (105 s of a 138 s job); pip cache never refreshes; mutable third-party action has write token; gh-pages commit message is a literal `$(date ...)`
findings.description: daily_refresh.yml runs `pip install -r requirements.txt` with the default PyPI torch, which on Linux is the CUDA build. Neither cloud_refresh nor the dashboard imports torch; the only non-NN importer is risk_monitor, and only for the IV inverter. Because requirements are unpinned and the cache key is hash(requirements.txt), the cache was saved once and never refreshed ('Cache hit ... not saving cache'), so new wheels are downloaded on every run. peaceiris/actions-gh-pages@v4 is a mutable third-party tag running with contents:write. Its commit_message input is not shell-expanded, so every gh-pages commit literally reads '$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)'. actions/checkout@v4, setup-python@v5 and cache@v4 trigger the Node 20 deprecation warning. tests.yml tests only 3.11 although README says 3.11+, and its comment still says '633 passed'. redeploy_site.sh force-pushes a fresh one-commit gh-pages from a local data_store, which contradicts the workflow's 'preserve gh-pages history' and can roll the site back to stale local data.
findings.evidence:
Job 114096310910 log: 'Downloading torch-2.14.1 ... (554.6 MB)', nvidia_cudnn_cu13 553.1 MB, nvidia_cublas 423.1 MB, nvidia_nccl_cu12 351.5 MB, triton 247.9 MB, cufft 214.1 MB, nccl_cu13 216.0 MB, cusolver 200.9 MB, plus others (~3.4 GB total).
Step timings: Install 01:20:28 -> 01:22:13 (105 s); cloud_refresh 16 s; job 138 s. 'Cache hit occurred on the primary key ..., not saving cache.'
`gh api .../commits?sha=gh-pages` shows 'Deploy 38012780844: $(date -u +%Y-%m-%d) 16a130a...'.
'##[warning]Node.js 20 is deprecated ... actions/cache@v4, actions/checkout@v4, actions/setup-python@v5'.
findings.proposed_fix: Split out requirements-nn.txt (torch) and requirements-dev.txt (pytest, ruff). Move the IV inverter out of nn_pricer so risk_monitor no longer imports torch. Install from a lock file and key the cache on the lock hash. Pin third-party actions to commit SHAs, or switch to actions/upload-pages-artifact + actions/deploy-pages with `pages: write, id-token: write`, and keep contents:write on a separate commit step. Compute the commit message in a prior step (`echo "msg=Deploy ${{ github.run_id }} $(date -u +%F)" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT`). Bump the actions to Node-24 majors. Add a 3.11/3.12/3.13 matrix to tests.yml. Delete or align redeploy_site.sh.

findings.title: Bot downloads an SPX chain every day and throws it away (DB not committed, parquet mirror gitignored), while the README's main limitation is 'no option history'
findings.description: cloud_refresh inserts the day's chain into data_store/vol_system.db and insert_options_snapshot mirrors it to data_store/parquet/, but the workflow commits only regime_labels.parquet and joint_cal_*.pkl, and data_store/parquet/ is gitignored. Every run therefore starts from the tracked DB, frozen at SPX 2026-06-18 with option snapshots 03-24/03-28/05-31/06-20, and the newly acquired chain is lost. The workflow comment 'The SQLite DB is NOT committed ... rebuilt fresh each run' is also wrong: the DB is not rebuilt, it is the stale tracked file plus a 400-day download. The project repeatedly names the lack of option history as its dominant limitation, and the data to fix it is being fetched and discarded every day.
findings.evidence:
Committed DB: options_snapshots dates = 2026-03-24, 03-28, 05-31, 06-20 only; spx_ohlcv max 2026-06-18.
CI log 2026-10-10: 'Inserted 2795 SPX options rows for 2026-10-09'; the commit step adds only 2 files ('create mode 100644 data_store/calibrations/joint_cal_2026-10-09.pkl').
Size check: a full 16,935-row chain is 327 KB as zstd parquet, so the bot's ~2-3k-row chains are about 50-60 KB/day.
findings.proposed_fix: Write each session's chain to data_store/options/spx_<session>.parquet (zstd), stop gitignoring that folder, and add it to the workflow's `git add`. Teach get_options_surface to read those files (or load them into a fresh DB at job start). Correct the workflow comment. Test: run cloud_refresh with a mocked yfinance chain and assert the parquet exists and round-trips through get_options_surface.

findings.title: Three parallel ingestion paths (cloud_refresh, DataPipeline.daily_refresh, yf_downloader._fetch_yf_options) disagree on expiries, filters, dates and idempotency; bugs fixed in one remain in the others
findings.evidence:
Code at the locations listed.
`git grep` shows DataPipeline is used only by dashboard/app.py:1255-1257.
The committed DB has 0 rows in vix_futures_daily and vix_futures_settlements: the CBOE paths have never produced data, and README.md:194 says 'CBOE CDN — 403 blocked'.
yfinance check today: ^VIX9D/^VIX3M/^VIX6M each return 28 rows for 2026-09-01..10-09 when the end date is inclusive.
findings.proposed_fix: Make one ingestion module (joint_vol_calibration/data/ingest.py) with fetch_spx_chain(session, max_dte, min_expiries) and refresh_market_data(start, end_inclusive). Name snapshots by session. Make inserts idempotent with a UNIQUE(snapshot_date, underlying, expiry, strike, right) constraint and INSERT OR REPLACE. Have cloud_refresh and the dashboard both call it. Delete the CBOE paths that never worked, or gate them behind a flag. Set HIST_END = None, meaning 'through the latest session'. Test: one fixture chain must go through both entry points and produce identical DB rows.

findings.title: No conftest isolation: tests read and write the tracked production DB and artifacts; regression guards are CWD-dependent source-text greps that missed the app.py relabel path
findings.description: There is no conftest.py and no pytest configuration. test_rates.py runs init_database() and inserts synthetic rows into the TRACKED vol_system.db and restores them in fixture teardown. That works for a normal run (checked: git status clean afterwards), but it is not atomic: SIGKILL, a CI timeout or OOM between the insert and teardown leaves the same synthetic T-bill rows that once became the published cash hurdle (15b4db5). Several C21 guards assert on source text: pathlib.Path('scripts/cloud_refresh.py').read_text() and inspect.getsource substrings. They fail from any other CWD, pass as long as a string is present, and by construction cannot see the same defect in other files (it is still in dashboard/app.py, see hygiene-dashboard-relabels-with-demoted-classifier). The walk-forward tests rerun the full XGBoost walk-forward 3 times with n_jobs=-1, which dominates runtime under contention. 4 class-scoped fixtures are defined as instance methods, which pytest deprecates for removal in 10.
findings.evidence:
`cd joint_vol_calibration && pytest tests/test_c21_audit_fixes.py -k 'bot_writes or rule_not_classifier'` gives 2 failed with FileNotFoundError: 'scripts/cloud_refresh.py'.
Full sweep (OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, -k 'not TestWalkForward'): 637 passed, 24 skipped, 5 deselected in 143 s, with 4x PytestRemovedIn10Warning 'Class-scoped fixture defined as instance method is deprecated'.
py-spy on a concurrent full run showed it spending its time in TestWalkForward._run_wf -> walk_forward_validation -> _retrain_classifier -> RegimeClassifier.fit.
All 24 skips are NN tests (weights and training cache gitignored), so the NN pricer, including the inverter above, is never exercised by CI.
findings.proposed_fix: Add joint_vol_calibration/tests/conftest.py with a session-scoped autouse fixture that copies data_store to tmp_path_factory and monkeypatches config.DATA_DIR, config.DB_PATH and database.DB_PATH (and the module-level DATA paths in dashboard/app.py) for all tests. Integration tests then read a copy and can never write the tracked files. Replace the source greps with behavioural tests: run cloud_refresh.recalibrate_heston and extend_regime_labels with monkeypatched yfinance and calibrator and assert DB rows and parquet contents. Use pathlib.Path(__file__).parents[2] for any repo paths. Make the WF result a class-scoped fixture with @classmethod and set XGBoost n_jobs from an env var in tests. Ship a tiny NN checkpoint (or train a 1-epoch model in a fixture) so the NN code path runs in CI.

findings.title: Published and docstring claims contradict the code: 'Carr-Madan FFT' (no FFT anywhere), heston_call_price 'undiscounted', 'Broadie-Kaya exact' MC, single-snapshot README rows, VIX-tenor cron rationale
findings.description:
Claims that do not match the code:
- README and substack say 'Carr-Madan FFT pricer'. No FFT is used anywhere (`grep np.fft|scipy.fft` finds nothing); pricing is quad/trapezoid integration of the damped integrand.
- heston_call_price says it returns an 'undiscounted call price (multiply by e^{-rT})', but it already discounts. Its alpha condition is wrong, and the n_integration_points argument is accepted and ignored (vulture 100%).
- heston_monte_carlo says 'Broadie-Kaya exact scheme', but it implements full-truncation Euler.
- pipeline.py says 'validate_no_lookahead() runs automated checks before any backtest'; nothing calls it, and it relies on `assert`, which python -O strips.
- database.py says 'Write functions are idempotent'; insert_options_snapshot is a plain INSERT.
- config.py says 'no magic numbers in model code', but BACKTEST_START/END (2018-01-02/2025-12-31) are unused and contradict 2018-01-01/2025-03-24, which are hard-coded in 4 other places.
- README rows 191/192/196/242 still say 'single snapshot 2026-03-24' while README:41 (fixed in 75b4844) says four snapshots, 61,815 rows. The prior fix was incomplete.
- The cron rationale says ^VIX9D/3M/6M exist 'ONLY as a current-day row', but Yahoo returns full history (28 daily rows for Sep 1–Oct 9).
- tests.yml says '633 passed'.
- latest_good_calibration_path's docstring says the fallback is 'newest sufficient file', but the code returns cals[-1] regardless of sufficiency.
- The rate label says 'USD 6M SOFR'.
findings.evidence:

findings.title: `with sqlite3.connect(...) as conn` never closes connections; Python 3.13 emits ResourceWarning on every query, and the dashboard leaks connections on error paths
findings.description: sqlite3.Connection's context manager only commits or rolls back. It does not close. All database.py helpers rely on garbage collection to close. Python 3.13 now warns about this, and in the long-running dashboard thread or under -W error it becomes noisy or failing. app.py's _db() connections are closed only on the happy path. The DB is also put in WAL mode on every connect and the tracked file is stored in WAL format (header bytes 18/19 = 2), so committing it while a -wal sidecar exists can capture a stale image.
findings.evidence: Python 3.13 venv: `get_spx_ohlcv(...); get_tbill_rate(...)` gives 'ResourceWarning: unclosed database in <sqlite3.Connection ...>' twice. Light subset (test_data_pipeline, test_lookahead, test_rates, test_c21) on 3.13 with -W default::ResourceWarning: 55 passed, 119 warnings, all unclosed-database. (Checked OK on 3.13: requirements install, freeze_site renders all 4 pages, and the same 55 tests pass with FutureWarning/DeprecationWarning as errors.)
findings.proposed_fix: Add `@contextmanager def _connect(): conn = sqlite3.connect(...); try: yield conn; conn.commit() finally: conn.close()` and use it everywhere, including app.py (`with closing(_db()) as con`). Run `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` and switch to journal_mode=DELETE before any commit of the DB. Add a 3.13 CI job with `-W error::ResourceWarning`.

findings.title: 129 print() calls in library modules; in CI their block-buffered stdout appears after later log lines, scrambling the job log
findings.description: Library code prints results: 53 calls in joint_calibrator, 32 in run_backtest, 19 in pdv, 16 in nn_pricer, 9 in quintic_calibrator. These go to block-buffered stdout while logging goes to stderr, so the GitHub log shows the calibration report after the run claims to be complete, which makes outage triage harder. quintic_calibrator's __main__ also runs warnings.filterwarnings('ignore') globally. config.LOG_LEVEL and LOG_DIR are defined, and LOG_DIR is created at import, but neither is used.
findings.evidence: Job 114096310910: '01:22:29 INFO Refresh complete. Site rebuilt at .site-build/' is followed by '[C4] Joint calibration: 2026-10-10 | S=7812 | 9 SPX opts ...', a block printed during step 3 at 01:22:18-25. Counts from `grep -rn '^\s*print(' joint_vol_calibration --include=*.py | grep -v tests`.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace print with logger.info, keeping verbose output behind logger levels. Configure logging once in the entry points (cloud_refresh, run_backtest, app __main__) using config.LOG_LEVEL. Run python with -u, or set PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 in the workflow env. Remove the global warnings.filterwarnings('ignore').

findings.title: scripts/backfill_calibration_provenance.py is not idempotent: re-running --apply would erase recorded provenance on every post-09-05 fit and disable the tenor gate for them
findings.description: The script overwrites n_spx_options and n_vix_tenors for EVERY joint_cal_*.pkl. Dates missing from its hard-coded CI_COUNTS table get None and 'legacy fit; data counts unrecorded', even when the pickle already holds counts recorded by the calibrator. is_acceptable_calibration skips the tenor gate when n_vix_tenors is None, so a re-run would un-gate fits.
findings.evidence: Dry run in a private copy prints '2026-09-11 tenors=None ... Would update 33 file(s)'. The actual 09-11 pickle holds n_spx_options=9, n_vix_tenors=4, spx_snapshot_date=2026-09-11.
findings.proposed_fix: Only fill keys that are absent (`cal.setdefault`) and skip files that already have provenance. Or delete the script now that the one-shot backfill is done. Test: run backfill(apply=True) twice on a tmp copy and assert the second run changes nothing, and that 09-11 keeps (9, 4).
